public_payload.normalized_proposition: Stopping model training would not make OpenAI and Anthropic profitable; inference is not a money-printer.

statement.excerpt: If stopping training was all that it’d take to turn these businesses profitable, they’d have done it already, because inference would be a money-printer rather than a cursed object eating away at Altman and Amodei’s souls.

our_interpretation: The testable financial reading is that removing training expenses alone would leave OpenAI and Anthropic unprofitable.
Hold contemporaneous revenue and non-training expenses constant. This does not assume that future revenue would survive indefinitely without new models.
Profitable refers to the whole business after remaining expenses, not merely a positive inference gross margin.
Use January through March 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter that evidence could report before the June 15 post. The post names no accounting period.
The claim does not specify an accounting basis. It remains unknown; strong financial scoring is therefore unavailable under the stated rules.
The assertion about what management would already have chosen is an argument, not independent evidence of the counterfactual financial result.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records for each company show a loss after removing only training expenses while retaining all other relevant expenses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that removing training expenses alone would produce a profit for either named company, with any difference between the companies reported explicitly.
